answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, time-delayed bond that only vests after weeks of attested work, so a shale of cheap new accounts cannot flood in overnight. Reputation then grows like a cipher: slow, verifiable, and hard to fake in bulk, because every claim must be countersigned by established peers who stake their own standing on it. A orchard of real, checkable deliverables anchors each account to costly history; one caught fake burns the bond and the endorsers' trust, so forging a thousand identities costs more than any of them can earn.
